messages:
alex: Heads up — ops flagged a regression risk when we nudge tenants off v1. Small tenants that are pinned + low volume are seeing big percentage cost changes. proposing a 'cost-anchor' exemption to soften the landing for ~30d.
maya: +1 to soft landing but need clear thresholds. what counts as 'small'? :thinking:
alex: my sketch: <=10 requests/day OR <=1k tokens/day for 7d rolling. exempted tenants kept on v1 route but flagged in console. exempt only once per tenant per sunset rollout.
jon: how would we record that in telemetry? we need to avoid double-counting tokens for billing vs migration metrics.
sara: can we add a migration tag so billing pipeline ignores anchor-exempt tokens for billing bump alerts but still tracks them for migration success?
alex: exactly. proposal: add header `X-Redwood-Migration-Anchor: true` on routed requests. telemetry pipeline can sample 100% of these and mark them for separate accounting. billing will not include them in "migration spike" alerts for 30d.
lucy: console UX: need a per-tenant badge + filter in the migration dashboard. PMs want a one-click revoke for anchors so CS can lift the exemption if customer asks.
jon: technical detail: routing order needs to prefer anchor-exempt pin before fallback to v2. current router checks pin -> version header -> fallback. we add anchor-check after pin but before fallback. pseudocode:
```
if pinned_version == "v1": route v1
else if anchor_exempt(tenant): route v1 and add header X-Redwood-Migration-Anchor:true
else route fallback
```

maya: what about quota interaction? pinned v1 tenants still consume shared quotas. if we exempt them and keep them on v1, could they block capacity for other tenants?
alex: good catch. exempted tenants get an "anchor soft-quota" limit: cap the per-minute RPS and token rate, lower than full v1 quota. prevents them from starving others.
sara: we should surface the anchor quota in the console billing/usage page and send a one-off notification when it's applied.
lucy: plus add a dashboard row: Anchor exemptions by tenant, started_at, expiry_at, applied_by, reason. filterable.
jon: ops concern: how does this affect autoscaling? if a lot of anchors exist, we might underprovision because we keep traffic on older pools. we should add a knob: global-anchor-cap at rollout time (percent of v1 capacity allowed for anchors).
ops-bot: Deploy-preview: routing change + header injection + anchor-flagging telemetry service built in staging. Runbook: check migration-rate, anchor-count, v1-utilization after deploy.
deploy-bot: CI looks good, smoke passed on staging, canary at 5% tomorrow. :rocket:
maya: sampling plan: we should 100% sample anchor traffic for the first week, then 10% after we verify metrics. need migration-success, token-delta, avg-latency, billing-delta. add alerts: billing-delta > 30% or v1-utilization > 70%.
alex: agree. implementation checklist: router change, header injection, telemetry tag, billing exclusion rule, console badge/filter, revoke action, global-anchor-cap flag, runbook. who wants which tasks?
sara: I can own console changes + badge + revoke API.
john: (typo) jon: I'll take the router + header + anchor flag logic.
maya: I'll own telemetry sampling + alert wiring.
lucy: I'll design dashboard rows and mock screenshots for the PM.
alex: cool. let's land the router change behind a feature flag `anchor-soft-landing` and run the canary tomorrow. ping here when the flag is on.
maya: noted. I'll add dashboard panels to track these metrics pre-canary. :eyes:
alex: thanks all — aim to have docs and runbook ready before canary. if anyone wants to block the anchor behavior we can kick it to a smaller cohort.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for 2024-05-14 09:00 UTC at 5%. Notifying oncall.
ops-bot: Runbook checklist posted: https://go/redwood/internal/runbooks/migration-anchor (staging).
